summary: Cleanup: orphaned demo clusters and legacy service accounts
description:
Issue summary: Several old demo Kubernetes clusters and a set of legacy service accounts associated with hackathon/poc work appear to be orphaned. These were created across multiple projects in 2023–2024 and are inflating resource listings and occasionally triggering alerts from billing monitors.

Impact: Low production risk but causes noise in billing dashboards, inventory confusion for on-call, and occasional IAM clutter that complicates permission audits.

Observed environment: staging clusters and a single us-east demo project. Affected resources include: kube clusters named demo-*, service accounts with prefixes hackathon- or poc-llm-*, and a handful of stale GKE node pools.

Steps to reproduce / find resources: 1) List clusters across projects via gcloud and filter by name patterns (demo-, hackathon-, poc-). 2) Cross-check service accounts via iam API for matching prefixes. 3) Confirm no recent bindings and no active pods/workloads. 4) Check billing tags and owner metadata for last-used timestamps.

Proposal / request: - Run a scoped inventory script to produce final list and owners. - For resources with no owner or owner unresponsive for 30 days, schedule a deletion window with a 7-day pre-delete notification. - Update inventory docs and add a short internal runbook for demo-cluster lifecycle and naming conventions.

Rollback / safety: Snapshot cluster metadata and export service-account IAM bindings prior to deletion. Ensure backups of any persisted test data are archived under shared_drives/engineering/_temp_uploads if needed.

Acceptance criteria: Inventory produced, owners contacted, at least 70% of orphaned clusters/accounts either reclaimed or scheduled for deletion, and runbook created in confluence/misc.
